answer: Divergent thread quarantine: every session emits a signed random seed into a shared commit log. Clones replay identical transcripts, so any two agents sharing a seed lineage get flagged and their outputs frozen. An attacker must fork a fresh seed for each clone and keep every branch consistent — one network fork per fake identity, not a copy. Honest agents diverge naturally, like paths through a meadow, so collisions stay rare; a voyage across seeds cannot be replayed. Cost: one fork plus ongoing divergence maintenance per clone.
